Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. Tigers primarily hunt deer, but as opportunistic predators, they can also eat wild boars, birds, fish, rodents, amphibians, reptiles, and even insects. I was filming this beautiful tigress when she went into labor. Witnessing the birth of this tiny white cub was a once-in-a-lifetime moment. 🙏 But our peace was shattered. A huge black wolf came out of the trees and went after the mother. I was terrified for them. 😥 Just when I thought the worst would happen, a cougar appeared! She stood her ground and bravely drove the wolf away. My heart was pounding. The cougar approached the crying cub, and I just held my breath, not knowing what she would do. Be Human Like a Tiger A tiger doesn't roar to prove strength. It moves in silence. It waits, watches, and chooses its moment. Not every battle is worth energy. A tiger walks alone-not because it's lonely, but because it trusts itself. Scars don't make it weaker; they remind it that it survived. When a tiger strikes, it commits fully. No hesitation. No doubt. It doesn't chase approval. The jungle already knows what it is. Life lesson: Move with purpose. Speak less, observe more. Protect your energy. Trust your power. Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.
